children: Australian stocks look set to add to their midweek decline, as worries over a potential October rate rise by the Fed weighed on U.S. equities. ASX futures are down by 0.3% ahead of Thursday's open, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 will head lower in early trade. The benchmark index lost 0.6% Wednesday, weighed by shares of major banks. Ahead of the open, regional lender Bank of Queensland held its dividend after reporting stronger-than-expected annual earnings. Software developer WiseTech Global said its cofounder would face no action from the country's securities regulator, which had been investigating his alleged share trading. The S&P 50 lost 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite shed 1.9%, and the DJIA gave up 0.1%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
